task: Build Zoo v1, the fifth and final minigame of the esl-likes 3D ESL game, as a complete playable slice: a walkable zoo with an entrance plaza and one looping path past six habitats; a visitor asks for help, the child asks 'What animal do you like?', hears 'I like elephants.', explores, frames and photographs that animal through a 2D viewfinder, returns and shows the photo; plus levels, listen-again, scoring, the saved stamp-book photo and the turnaround. The shared shell, speech stack and the other four minigames already exist and work; this order adds one minigame against the frozen interface.
requirements: Read SPEC.md first: the anti-shortcut rule near the top, section 3 ('Listening again'), and section 8 (Zoo v1), which is the frozen design and wins over any assumption. Read DESIGN_DECISIONS.md for existing rationale (especially the 2026-09-12 Zoo entry). Do not modify SPEC.md.

Create src/minigames/zoo/ with at least index.js (createZoo(ctx) controller), scoring.js (PURE logic, no DOM, no three.js) and scoring.test.mjs (node:test). Further modules are welcome (world building, animals, viewfinder).

createZoo(ctx) implements the frozen interface { id, enter(level), update(dt), exit() } exactly as src/minigames/restaurant/index.js does, including the same level resolution (enter(level) falling back to settings 'difficulty', clamped 1..3) and the settings subscription for micFree / textSize.

Register it: src/main.js minigames map gets ['zoo', createZoo]; in src/config/lesson.js set the zoo lesson available: true and add a UI.zoo block with ALL new Japanese strings. No UI text hardcoded elsewhere. Visitor answers come only from answerFor(LESSON, animalId).

World per SPEC 8: an entrance plaza where visitors wait, and ONE looping path that passes all six habitats and returns to the plaza. Each habitat holds a slow-moving procedural blocky animal (elephant, lion, panda, monkey, giraffe, penguin — recognisable by silhouette and colour) and a large sign with a picture and the English word, readable at 1366x768. Landmarks (plaza fountain, tall tree, striped gate) aid orientation. Large but crossable; a child must never feel lost. Habitat positions are FIXED (not shuffled).

Controls and camera as in the Restaurant: WASD/arrows with its movement feel (heading atan2(move.x, -move.y), shortest-way turning) and a follow camera DIRECTLY BEHIND the avatar (no sideways offset — an off-axis follow camera made Sports' controls feel diagonal and had to be fixed). Generous proximity to talk to a waiting visitor via promptQuestion(ctx, LESSON, { isActive, onAccepted }) from src/systems/speechPrompt.js. No mouse-look, no pointer lock, no manual camera rotation outside the viewfinder.

Loop per SPEC 8: visitors wait at random plaza spots; asked -> answer via ctx.dialogue with answerFor(LESSON, animal) (spoken + bubble), bubble then disappears; no ticket, icon, marker, arrow, minimap or persistent text of the answer anywhere. The child explores, photographs an animal, returns to the visitor and presses Space to show the photo. Correct animal: delighted reaction (emote-yes, happy Japanese line), the visitor leaves, the next request begins. Wrong animal: a Japanese line saying it is not their favourite, with NO English repeat; the visitor waits for another try.

Photo mechanic per SPEC 8: a camera control (button plus a key, keyboard-reachable) opens a 2D viewfinder overlay over the 3D view, with a visible frame and a shutter button. Aiming is coarse and forgiving: turn and step, never pixel-accurate, no mouse-look. The shutter only works when an animal is reasonably centred and large enough in the frame; show clearly (framing guide plus an enabled/disabled shutter) when it is ready. Taking a photo stores ONE photo: a new shot replaces the previous one. Keep a small visible indicator of which photo is currently carried. Closing the viewfinder returns to normal play with movement and camera restored, under the shared wipe where a seam would otherwise show.

Listening again (SPEC 3): the shared createListenAgain({ root, label: UI.listenAgain, onPress }) from src/ui/listenAgain.js is shown while a request is open; pressing it replays that visitor's exact answer sentence (and each waiting visitor's in turn at L2/L3) and marks them replayed. Never on Space, never deducts normal credit.
Difficulty per SPEC 8: L1 3 requests one visitor at a time; L2 4 requests with two visitors waiting; L3 6 requests with three. No timer, no patience meter, no failure state.

Anti-shortcut per SPEC 8: each visitor's animal uniformly random over all six, independent of model, spot, asking order and other visitors; repeats allowed (pure seedable pickAnimal(rng) in scoring.js). Visitors carry nothing animal-related; no habitat is highlighted; nothing points the way.
Visitor models: any Kenney key except characters.playerModel ('a'), random per visitor; do NOT tint textured Kenney models. Kenney models face +z at rotation.y = 0.

Scoring in scoring.js: pure scoreSession(records) where each record is { outcome: 'first' | 'later', framing: 0..1, replayed: boolean }. 'first' = the first photo shown for that request was the right animal. Points: first 5, later 2; + 2 * framing when correct; +1 memory bonus if never replayed. ratio = earned / (8 * count). Stars: >= 0.75 -> 3, >= 0.4 -> 2, else 1; first-try share < 0.5 can never give 3 stars. framing is a pure measure of how centred and large the animal was in the frame at shutter time, computed in scoring.js from normalised frame coordinates.

scoring.test.mjs must cover at least: all first-try with good framing and no replays -> 3 stars; the same but every visitor replayed -> still 3 stars; first-try share below half never gives 3 stars; poor framing scores lower than good framing but never below 1 star; a seeded 'show every animal in turn' simulation reaches 3 stars in under 1% of sessions; pickAnimal over several hundred seeded draws covers all six; the framing measure is symmetric and peaks at a centred, well-sized subject.

The photo: the kept snapshot must be a data: URL image of the framed shot, passed out at the end via finish({ stars, detail: { category: 'animal', answer, zooPhoto } }) — src/main.js already forwards detail.zooPhoto to progression.setZooPhoto, and src/ui/stampBook.js already renders it for the zoo stamp. Keep it small (a modest resolution, JPEG or PNG under roughly 200 kB) so localStorage does not overflow; if a save would be too large, prefer a smaller image rather than failing.

Turnaround after the last request: a zookeeper or the last visitor asks via promptAnswer(ctx, LESSON, ...) with all six animals, framed as a grounded, readable side-on two-shot in which the avatar never hides the speaker, then finish(...) as above.

Test hooks: stable DOM class names for the minigame's own overlay (at least an instruction element, a notice element, the viewfinder root, the shutter button and the carried-photo indicator), and a READ-ONLY window.__eslDebug.zoo getter returning { phase, level, player: { x, z }, habitats: [{ id, x, z }], visitors: [{ state, asked, served, x, z }], carriedPhoto: <animal id or null>, shutterReady: boolean }. It must NOT expose visitors' wanted animals. Remove it in exit().

exit() disposes every owned geometry, material, texture and canvas, removes overlays, listeners, injected styles and the debug hook, and clears speech/hud targets, exactly as the Restaurant does. Entering Zoo twice from the hub must not leak or duplicate anything.

npm test and npm run build must both pass. Capture your own 1366x768 screenshots of: the plaza on entry, a visitor answering, the looping path with a habitat sign, the viewfinder with the shutter not yet ready, the viewfinder ready to shoot, showing the photo to a visitor, and the turnaround; state what you checked in them.
constraints: Do NOT modify SPEC.md, src/systems/*, src/ui/*, src/scenes/hub.js, src/styles.css, scripts/, or any other minigame. If a shared system genuinely lacks something, say so in the summary instead of editing it. The only shared edits allowed: the registry line and import in src/main.js, and in src/config/lesson.js the zoo `available` flag plus a new UI.zoo block.
Do NOT add dependencies. three and vite only.
Do NOT build a universal minigame base class or share scoring maths with other minigames.
Do NOT add any marker, arrow, compass, minimap or highlight that points at the wanted habitat.

Source-edit hygiene: edit files with structured file tools. If a shell-based edit fails on quoting or escaping, stop editing through the shell for that change and use the file tools; never escalate through nested shell/python/regex patches.
Do not inline code into shell commands; run the declared npm scripts.
notes: Governing rule (SPEC): the NPC's English answer must be information the child needs. For the Zoo: a child who ignores 'I like pandas.' can still finish by touring habitats and showing photos one at a time (never stuck) but can never reliably get three stars, because the camera holds only one photo and a wrong showing loses the dominant first-try credit. In your summary, state how each anti-shortcut leak in SPEC was checked (fixed mapping, order, elimination, colour/appearance cues, default selection, free trial-and-error). Tone: the calm, exploratory finale — the reward is the zoo itself and the photo in the stamp book. Composition note: this order is deliberately atomic. The viewfinder, the animals and the scoring are coupled through the same scene objects, and splitting them would need a frozen interface between halves and risk two workers editing one controller. Lessons already paid for in this project, apply them up front: characters and their bubbles must never be hidden behind scenery or the avatar; the follow camera belongs directly behind the avatar or the controls feel diagonal; signs must be large and readable; anything asking the turnaround must stand on a real floor; the shared dialogue bubble now balances its lines, so keep Japanese strings phrase-spaced. Known traps: Kenney models face +z; one avatar key; tinting textured Kenney models turns skin grey; focused buttons must not swallow movement keys (handled in input.js). Restaurant is the reference for movement, follow camera, proximity talk and exit() hygiene; Coloring for a full-screen 2D overlay under the shared wipe and for canvas work; Drink Stand and Sports for signs, listen-again targeting, the debug hook and the two-shot. Append meaningful design decisions to DESIGN_DECISIONS.md as dated entries. List every file you touched.
